study.question: Does the hybrid's small validation advantage require g0 token content in event-addressing queries or learned terminal event weights, or can an active low-rank residual on a simple historical mean or the inherited DIN sum reproduce it? The current incumbent g1-r0007-state_uniform_none scores 0.8307177422018418 versus g0's 0.8301982212762624, but costs 947.02 versus 443.35 training seconds; its purchase AUC is lower by 0.00167493 and click AUC by 0.00018044. These single-seed results motivate attribution before adding another mechanism.
study.hypothesis: The remaining learned terminal event-addressing operation may provide complementary history information after uniform reading of g0 state. If its advantage specifically comes from compatibility with g0 representation content, intact-state adaptive pooling should beat the identity-state adaptive replacement. If learned event selection matters, it should also beat masked-mean pooling. Conversely, mean or DIN replacements matching or exceeding the intact hybrid would favor simpler summary/optimization explanations for this tested gain. This is a discriminating replacement study; no new general attention mechanism, novelty, additivity of source gains, or expected performance improvement is asserted.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit its complete field/relation/position and feedback representation, shared JointBlock and original towers. The hybrid adds a zero-start transformed wide historical summary. This study changes only what feeds that residual branch, retaining g0 tower inputs.
Exact source is replayed byte-for-byte. New arms replace terminal event weights or token content used only by the residual branch; all modules, shapes, loss and initialization remain inherited.

The source uses evolving feature queries and target-match addressing. The tested hybrid retains task queries and a wide raw-value read after g0 interaction. Terminal match priors remain disabled following local negative transfer.

Archived primary text lines 271-277 explains retaining unnormalized interest intensity. The DIN residual control transforms the inherited signed sum rather than introducing a second normalized event summary; it is not an exact DIN reproduction.

Primary paper uses global feature-derived queries, sequence decoding and query boosting; pinned benchmark forward inspected separately. Here g0 tokens remain read-only, followed by a single wide event summary. No HyFormer sequence encoder or boosting implementation is adopted.

Primary paper describes fixed and feature-conditioned interest queries and heterogeneous mixing. Identity-state replacement supplies a local fixed/task-and-occupancy query control; no global versus real-time sequence split or HeteroMixer is imported.

Primary paper alternates feature-query mixing, sequence attention and fusion. This study neither co-updates event tokens nor adopts its mixer. It tests whether content-conditioned terminal selection is necessary in this existing hybrid.

inherited_components: All g0 model code except adding the already committed hybrid branch call; 25 incumbent methods unchanged in new modules
Existing task identities, two narrow task mixers, Q/K/V maps, raw event projection and rank embeddings
Original 112-to-32-to-112 bias-free maps, nonaffine LayerNorm and zero-start 112-to-112 residual output at default dimensions
Exact masking, null handling, current-action sanitization and frozen four-task sum-BCE host training
Incumbent uniform structured-state reads, disabled terminal prior, same module construction/RNG isolation and all original prediction towers
study.proposed_difference: Submit one masked-mean residual candidate and three controls. mean_residual supplies a convex uniform mean of valid raw historical values to the existing low-rank normalized residual. identity_attention replaces only the branch's final g0 tokens with existing learned token identities, preserving the exact token-valid mask, seed/refinement structure, task identities and adaptive event weights; intact g0 tokens still enter every prediction tower. din_reparameterization supplies the already computed global signed DIN sum to the same residual transformation, with no second learned selection. incumbent_replay is the exact committed source. In replacement modules adaptive event scores, narrow reads and match computations remain executed, so this is attribution before pruning. No uniform-by-identity fourth factorial cell is trained: when terminal weights are uniform, queries cannot affect the value summary, making that cell structurally redundant.
predictions: If g0 state content contributes specifically through the new event-addressing branch, incumbent_replay should exceed identity_attention on validation macro AUC under the same seed and host recipe. Otherwise the tested content-conditioned compatibility hypothesis lacks support.

If learned terminal selection contributes beyond a simple extra mean-history channel, incumbent_replay should exceed mean_residual. Similar performance would favor removal of adaptive retrieval in a later pruned, measured implementation.

If additional residual parameterization of information already available to the tower explains the gain, din_reparameterization should reproduce the improvement over g0 and approach the incumbent. Mean outperforming DIN would instead motivate a narrower normalized/raw-summary hypothesis; that contrast alone does not isolate normalization from weighting.
Identity-adaptive queries retain task identity and temporal-bin presence, so they may still exploit generic task/history preference through event keys. They are not sample-information-free queries.

Report macro AUC and Logloss, all four task deltas against DIN, g0, the g1 source and incumbent. History slices remain empty, 1-16, 17-64, >64 with counts; no slice selects checkpoints. Empty-history predictions within trained arms can differ through shared training even though branch outputs are forced to zero for empty histories.
falsifiers: An identity-only branch matching or beating the intact incumbent opposes the claim that per-sample g0 state content is necessary for this branch under the tested protocol.
A uniform mean matching or beating the intact incumbent opposes a learned-terminal-weight explanation of the observed hybrid gain.

A DIN reparameterization matching the hybrid and beating g0 weakens a complementary-retrieval explanation and favors added residual capacity or optimization. No single-seed near-tie is called equivalence or significance.

Failure to exceed g0 on repetitions, or unexplained replay/parity discrepancies, prevents a repeatable added-utility conclusion. A failed numerical preflight is an implementation failure, not scientific counterevidence.
alternative_explanations: One-seed checkpoint selection, sampling variation, and cumulative validation selection can account for the small gain; repeated seeds do not identify a mechanism.

Added low-rank residual capacity, output normalization, optimization conditioning, shared embedding gradients or branch-specific backward paths can explain gains without representation-interaction complementarity.

Equal nominal parameters do not imply equal expressive capacity: uniform and DIN replacements deactivate query dependence and share the residual summary across tasks; identity replacement retains occupancy information. Effective gradient-active capacity and measured backward cost must be reported.

DIN versus mean changes signed weights, aggregate scale, and target dependence together. This is a replacement control, not an isolated test of normalization or intensity; a future scale/weight factorial would be needed.
Single-pass training may favor one residual parameterization. Identical data passes support mechanism comparisons, not equal-compute efficiency claims.

Observed cart/favorite gains and purchase/click regressions can cancel in macro AUC; auxiliary labels are user/category/brand matches within 24h, not advertisement-specific conversions. Offline feedback visibility and vocabulary construction limit production transfer.

trajectory_interpretation: Baseline DIN establishes the initial reference at 0.8099233881; g0 supplies a much stronger representation baseline at 0.8301982213.
Original g1 match-terminal source scores 0.8192325306, below g0. Its gains cannot be added to g0.
Round 6 hybrid with no prior beats its adaptive, uniform and rotated priors. Thus terminal match prior transfer was unsuccessful here; do not revive it without new evidence.

Round 7 state refinement beats event refinement modestly, but state adaptive does not beat state uniform, and either terminal-prior arm regresses. No learned structured-state routing advantage is established.
